assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and the incretin-based therapies built on it changed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity and opened cardiometabolic, renal and possibly neurological indications. The discovery chain runs from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36), through its short half-life and degradation by DPP-4, to long-acting analogues. The change in the field and in medicine is large and still growing.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology, secretion and clinical effects of GLP-1) and Drucker (receptor biology, GLP-2 and the gut-pancreas axis, translational framing) are the clearest scientific contributors. Knudsen led the design of the long-acting acylated analogues (liraglutide, then semaglutide) that made the biology a drug. Mojsov's contribution in identifying and characterizing the active GLP-1 peptide is credited but disputed, and the allocation between her and the other names is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently over decades by clinical outcome trials and very wide clinical use. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue. Interpretation is stable, although the newer non-metabolic indications are still being established.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among Drucker, Holst, Knudsen and Mojsov is contested; the three-person limit forces exclusion of a plausible contributor.
Whether the committee prefers to honor the physiology or the drug development is unclear.
I am relying on my own recollection of the discovery history and have not verified the credit claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells directed by chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and more recently show promise in autoimmune disease. The concept is original, the clinical effect is striking and the field of cell therapy has been reshaped by it.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed the design of second-generation CAR constructs with costimulation and early preclinical proof. June led the first successful clinical translation in CLL and pediatric ALL. Rosenberg pioneered adoptive T-cell therapy and early gene-modified T-cell trials. Other groups (Eshhar, Finney, Brentjens, Gross) made early construct contributions, and the supplied credit omits them, so the fairness of this trio is not settled.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products, independent replication across centers and multi-year remissions support maturity. Long-term safety, solid-tumor limits and manufacturing constraints remain, but the core discovery is stable.
uncertainties: Early CAR concept credit (for example the first chimeric receptor designs) lies outside the supplied names.
Rosenberg's role may be better described as adoptive cell transfer in general than CAR-T specifically.
Facts on first-in-human timelines are from memory and not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Recombinant L1 virus-like particle vaccines against HPV prevent persistent infection, cervical precancer and are now reducing cervical cancer incidence in vaccinated cohorts. This is a clear, original and highly consequential discovery with global preventive impact, and it follows naturally on the earlier recognition of HPV as a cause of cervical cancer.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller showed that L1 self-assembles into VLPs that induce neutralizing antibodies; Frazer and colleagues independently achieved VLP formation and moved the vaccine toward the clinic. Zhou and others are also associated with the Frazer work, and the supplied credit of three people appears workable, though the relative weight of independent parallel work is open.
assessment.maturity: Population-level efficacy against cervical cancer is now documented in several countries. Confirmation is strong and the timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Allocation among parallel VLP efforts (including the late Jian Zhou) may be contested.
Commercial development involved many contributors not in the credited set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of tau in Alzheimer paired helical filaments and of alpha-synuclein in Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites established the molecular identity of the main inclusions of neurodegeneration and unified these disorders as proteinopathies. It underpins current biomarkers, structural work on filament folds and many therapeutic programs.
assessment.attribution: Goedert and Spillantini are the two credited names, with a clear and relatively compact set of decisive observations (tau in filaments; alpha-synuclein in Lewy bodies in 1997). A two-person prize is feasible. Contributions by others on tau (Kosik, Ihara, Wischik, Brion) and on alpha-synuclein genetics (Polymeropoulos) are outside the credit and may complicate fairness.
assessment.maturity: Findings are replicated and the proteinopathy concept is broadly accepted. A clear therapeutic payoff is still pending, which makes the discovery impactful in concept but less so clinically; whether this suggests timeliness or prematurity is a judgment call.
uncertainties: Debated causal role of aggregates versus other pathology.
Priority claims on tau filament composition by other groups are not captured in the credited names.
Spillantini's participation is subject to the usual attribution complexities of the alpha-synuclein story, which I cannot verify here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides that raise SMN2 exon 7 inclusion led to nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, which transformed a lethal infantile disease. It is a clear mechanism-to-medicine story and established antisense splicing correction as a therapeutic platform.
assessment.attribution: Krainer identified the splicing silencer elements and guided the target; Bennett and the Ionis team developed the chemistry and drug. Both are credited, and a two-person prize is plausible. Others (Hua, Singh, Adrian Krainer's collaborators, and the clinical team led by Finkel and others) are not part of the proposed set.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with extensive long-term clinical data, and the platform has been replicated for other disorders. Recognition would be timely, though the discovery is somewhat narrower than the largest candidates.
uncertainties: The relative weight of the basic splicing discovery versus oligonucleotide drug chemistry.
Contributions of other splice-switching pioneers (Kole, Dominski) are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of BCL11A as the repressor of fetal hemoglobin and its use as a therapeutic target led to the first CRISPR-based therapy approved for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia. It is a strong example of human genetics-informed target discovery coupled to genome editing.
assessment.attribution: Orkin and Sankaran carried the original mechanistic work, with GWAS-based pointers from others (Menzel, Thein, Lettre) and the enhancer-editing strategy developed by Bauer and Orkin. Thein's genetic association work is plausible to credit and is one of the unresolved allocation issues. I propose the three who built the mechanism and the therapeutic edit.
assessment.maturity: Clinical approval is recent and long-term outcomes are still accumulating, though initial efficacy is strong. Likely a little early compared with the very mature candidates above.
uncertainties: Genome-editing credit (CRISPR) would probably be treated separately and already received a Chemistry prize.
Long-term safety and access are not yet known.
Allocation among Orkin, Sankaran, Bauer and Thein is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signaling, with IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing and later PERK and ATF6 arms, and is relevant in diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and secretory-cell physiology. It is an original and clear concept with lasting impact on cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the decisive names for the discovery of IRE1-mediated signaling and the transcriptional program, with Walter's work on the pathway's mechanism and Mori's on the transcriptional response. Others such as Ron and Harding (PERK/eIF2alpha) and Sidrauski are relevant to the broader UPR, and the credited pair covers the core pathway only partially. Probably a fair and workable two-person claim for the ER-to-nucleus signal.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is well established and widely reproduced for decades. The therapeutic translation (for instance ISRIB or related) is still developing, which makes the case basic-science heavy but timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would require a stronger clinical link.
The PERK arm contributors are outside the credited names and could change the fairness of the configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a way to control defined cells with light, and it has transformed circuit-level causal study across the brain and other organs. The tool-based change in the field is large and lasting, although the direct medical impact is still modest (early retinal applications).
assessment.attribution: Credit is highly distributed. Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann identified and characterized channelrhodopsins, while Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenboeck established genetically targeted neural use. With a three-laureate limit, I propose the combination that spans the discovery of the channel and its use in neurons, but this excludes Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck and is unlikely to be uncontroversial.
assessment.maturity: Very widely used and replicated. Recognition is timely, but the physiology-or-medicine fit is tool-based and clinical translation is still early.
uncertainties: The attribution configuration is hard and may be the main obstacle.
Whether a methodological tool fits the prize intent better than a discovery-driven finding is an open question for the committee.
